newsitem.title: PERU: Lima share prices end up on long-term buys.
newsitem.headline: Lima share prices end up on long-term buys.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed up Friday for the third consecutive session as investors bought companies' stocks believed to have solid long-term prospects, brokers said.
The market was expected to climb again Monday with the economy's strong growth potential attracting players to buy shares in the mining and consumer sectors, they added.
Friday, the General Index IGRA rose 0.63 percent to 2,144.7 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index ISEL gained 0.98 percent to 3,086.1 points.
In a total of 2,298 trades, volume was 50.9 million soles ($19.2 million), brokers said.

"Investors are betting on the long-term, especially on the mining and massive consumption sectors -- in the case of the former, because of the expectations for metal prices, and in the case of the latter, due to the country's economic panorama," Miguel Bondy of local brokerage Andino Capital Market, said.
Peru's largest brewery group Union de Cervecerias Peruanas Backus y Johnston SA gained 1.92 percent to 2.65 soles on strong volume of 2.7 million shares.
Chocolate producer D'Onofrio climbed 4.07 percent to close at 1.28 soles on volume of 292,000 shares.
Polymetallic miner Morococha climbed 3.33 percent to close at 6.20 soles on 114,000 shares.
Benchmark Telefonica del Peru bucked Friday's trend and continued its run of low volumes. The telecom company ended down 1.02 percent at 6.76 soles on volume of 336,000 shares.
